instruction:
Rotate Middle Arm, Preserve End-Effector World Position `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend` contains three mesh objects `Arm1`, `Arm2`, `Arm3` in a parent chain. Launch Blender by running `blender` from a terminal. Before starting the work, use `/opt/blender/blender` for Blender command-line or background runs when working on `scene.blend`.

Rotate `Arm2` by +30 degrees around its own local Z axis, then adjust only `Arm3.location` so `Arm3` keeps exactly the same world-space position it had in the supplied scene. Save the result as `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`. ## Requirements 1. `Arm1`, `Arm2`, `Arm3` all exist as mesh objects in the output. 2. Parent chain is intact: `Arm1` has no parent, `Arm2.parent == Arm1`, `Arm3.parent == Arm2`. 3. `Arm1`'s world transform matches the supplied scene. 4. `Arm2` keeps the same world position as in the supplied scene, while only its local Z rotation changes by pi/6 and its local X/Y values stay unchanged. 5. `Arm3`'s world position matches its position in the supplied scene to within Euclidean distance 5e-3.
